correctness.rationale: For every \(N\ge4\) and \(p\in[0,1]\) a Schmidt-rank cut argument rules out two perfect Bell outputs sharing an edge while swapping realizes every set of disjoint open paths. The three four-endpoint pairings then give conditional deficits 0, (g2+min(g1,g3))p^s, and g2 p^s, respectively. Every ordered positive-gap triple of span s translates N-s times, proving the finite polynomial. Independent positive-composition sums give the parity coefficients, an absolutely convergent generating function gives the fixed-\(p\) \(N^{-3}\) constant, and uniform cubic coefficient growth plus Riemann sums proves the \(p_N=e^{-\lambda/N}\) crossover. The integrand is positive, strictly decreasing in lambda, and has exact endpoint 1/2 and large-lambda behavior \(4/\lambda^2\). Standard-library rational exhaustive enumeration checks \(N=4,\ldots,8\), but is not used as an all-N proof. No relaxed-fidelity or physical-layer conclusion is made.

evidence: arXiv:2609.39690v1 Theorem 1 and Appendix C Eqs. (11)--(13), (40)--(41), pp. 11 and 23--25, allow arbitrary even numbers of active users and fixed link multiplicity, and prove fixed-success-probability order bounds.
The present calculation specializes those broad definitions to \(M=4\) and \(w=W=1\); it adds an explicit conditional contention calculation and a nonuniform limit under \(p_N=e^{-\lambda/N}\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier interval integer program is strictly broader as an unevaluated optimization, so its cut characterization, existence of the capacity, and fixed-p scaling are not new. However its published fixed-p asymptotic cannot be substituted into the p_N varying regime, and the complete closed polynomial coefficients and sharp crossover require separate analytical summation and asymptotics. The new contribution is assessed as that exact evaluation, not as a new general capacity theory.

originality.rationale: The general integer interval program and leading fixed-link transport order in arXiv:2609.39690v1 are prior results and explicitly credited. The final claim is its evaluated random-four-user Bernoulli expectation, exact contention coefficients and \(N^{-3}\) constant, together with a nonuniform near-perfect-link crossover that fixed-\(p\) asymptotics do not resolve. The primary source full text and relevant multipath literature were compared; the recorded mathematical-record queries found no statement of the same evaluated formulas. Implicit earlier equivalence remains a stated priority risk.
residual_risks: The general Eq. (41) implies computational recovery of this special case, so originality is strictly in its explicit analytic evaluation and new limit rather than in the cut theorem.
An unindexed or unpublished earlier solution of the same random four-user interval-packing sum may exist.
The 2024 alternative optimization article was only partially read in this session; its reported setting differs.

value.rationale: Four active users are the first nontrivial uniform exclusive-pairing case with possible shared-edge competition. The all-size formula isolates an exact strictly positive contention penalty, including its sharp \(N^{-3}\) decay at fixed p, and shows that this small-penalty expansion is nonuniform as \(p\to1\): an explicit capacity of order a_N N with a monotone crossover replaces it. This is a natural missing finite-system analysis and singular parameter boundary of the recent model, not an arbitrary small numerical improvement or a known table computation.
